instruction: Repair the supplied Python implementation of solve(data). Implement solve(data). defaults is an array of report codes enabled by the organization. layers is an array of overrides in order from the broadest region to the most local site. Each layer has state, enable and disable fields. Apply only layers with state 'active'. For each active layer, enable all codes in its enable array, then remove all codes in its disable array from the entire effective set. A disable wins a conflict within the same layer. A later active layer may re-enable a previously disabled code. Codes are case-sensitive nonempty ASCII strings. Repeated codes have one membership, and removing an absent code has no effect. Return the final enabled codes once each, sorted by ascending ASCII order.

Repair the supplied Python implementation of solve(data). Given an invoice revision ID in `head` and an unordered list `revisions`, return the ID of the nearest issued revision on the chain from `head`, including `head` itself. Each revision has a unique string `id`, a `supersedes` field containing an older revision ID or null, and a `state` of `issued` or `voided`. A voided revision is ineligible, but its link to the older revision remains valid. Follow only the links from `head`. Chain distance determines priority regardless of list order or ID spelling. Return {"id": null} if the chain contains no issued revision or `head` is null. All non-null references exist and chains are acyclic.

Repair the supplied Python implementation of solve(data). Implement solve(data) for a document excerpt builder. paragraphs is a list of strings. citations is a list of objects with id, paragraph, start and end. ranges is a list of objects with paragraph, start, end and state. Paragraph indices are zero-based. All offsets count Unicode code points, and all intervals are half-open and within their paragraph. Process ranges with state 'selected' and positive length in request order. Preserve repeated selections and every character of each slice. Join slices with one newline between consecutive slices. For each slice, clip every citation from the same paragraph to its intersection with that slice. Emit each positive-length intersection as {id,start,end} with offsets into the joined text. Within each slice, emit citations in their original input order. Return {text,citations}, including an empty string and empty list when nothing is selected.

Repair the supplied Python implementation of solve(data). Repair solve(data) for a map annotation importer. The positive integers width and height describe the source tile in pixels. The viewer rotates the tile clockwise by rotation degrees, one of 0, 90, 180, or 270. Each entry in points is an integer pair [x, y] measured on the rotated display, with origin at the top left, x increasing rightward, and y increasing downward. Return the corresponding source pixel pairs in input order, preserving duplicates. Return null in place of any point outside the displayed tile. Pixel indices start at zero and exclude the width and height endpoints. Quarter turns swap the displayed width and height. There is no scaling or interpolation.
